Opinion.summary: The current regulation should be maintained because the proposed amendment infringes upon parents' rights to express opinions (ⓐ) and unjustly discriminates against students receiving other measures (ⓑ).

c1.text: Parents have the right to participate in the educational process of their underage children.

c2.text: When the school imposes a disadvantageous measure on a student, parents have the right to express their opinion on the matter.

c3.text: The proposed amendment allows appeals only in cases of transfer and expulsion measures.

c4.text: ⓐ The proposed amendment infringes upon parents' right to express opinions regarding disadvantageous measures.

c5.text: The proposed amendment permits appeals only to perpetrating students who have received transfer or expulsion measures.

c6.text: ⓑ The proposed amendment results in the unjust discrimination of other perpetrating students and their guardians who have received other measures.

c7.text: The current regulation should be maintained.

a.note: Alternative legal remedies provide an argument attacking c4, so c4 is weakened rather than strengthened.

b.note: Unrestorable harm provides a ground for reasonable differentiation, attacking c6.

c.note: The responsibility for student growth provides further support for c4 and c6, so c4 is not weakened.

h1.text: Legal remedies are available by other means for measures for which appeals are not permitted.

h2.text: Parents can seek relief through other legal remedies, so the proposed amendment does not infringe upon their right to express opinions.

h3.text: The harm suffered by perpetrating students due to transfer or expulsion cannot be restored even if overturned in a lawsuit, unlike with other measures.

h4.text: Allowing appeals only for transfer and expulsion measures is a reasonable differentiation, not unjust discrimination.

h5.text: It is the responsibility of schools and society to ensure that all perpetrating students are given the opportunity to appeal and thereby grow into exemplary members of society.

h6.text: All perpetrating students and their parents should be given an opportunity to appeal, so denying appeals for other measures infringes parents' rights and unjustly discriminates.
